recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if the work group wants a new policy forbidding narrative-only List instances entirely or wants new non-normative examples distinguishing List from other narrative-bearing resources.
issue_request: FHIR-7372 was Published with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification. It objected to List scope wording that said List content might be narrative only, such as a text record of family history, because some narrative document sections should not be called Lists. The final disposition said to see FHIR-7371.
initial_application: No Jira-tagged source commit for FHIR-7372 or FHIR-7371 was found. The challenged List introduction wording came from earlier commit d72b1d787a for collection-type clarification, and FHIR-7371 comments say the concern became redundant after Composition was reworked.
additional_context: FHIR-7371 carries the paired request that narrative-only content should not use List unless it is actually a collection/list. Current active source now separates the cases: List is a flat collection with optional entries, narrative-only document sections are represented by Composition.section.text with no Composition.section.entry, and document presentation/attestation is based on Composition and section narratives rather than List.text.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source no longer forces non-list narrative document sections through List, and the remaining List introduction sentence is still valid for genuine List instances whose curated collection is represented only in narrative.

related_jiras.note: FHIR-7372 explicitly defers to the paired narrative-only List issue.
A later reconciliation commit aligned current List notes and Composition document narrative guidance with the section.text model.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Not Persuasive with Modification issue objecting to List scope wording about narrative-only family-history content and deferring to FHIR-7371.
evidence_items.learned: The seed is final and should be interpreted through the paired FHIR-7371 Composition/List disposition.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Not Persuasive with Modification paired issue saying non-list narrative such as Chief Complaint should not use List and noting the concern became redundant after Composition changes.
evidence_items.learned: The approved intent was to stop forcing non-list document narrative into List, not to forbid all narrative-only List instances.

evidence_items.summary: List is described as a flat collection, List.entry is optional, and List notes direct narrative-only document sections to Composition.section.text with no Composition.section.entry.
evidence_items.learned: The active List source supports genuine narrative-only Lists while avoiding the old document-section overuse problem.

evidence_items.summary: Composition.section.text carries attested section narrative, section.entry is optional, and document presentation uses subject, Composition, and section.text narratives.
evidence_items.learned: Current Composition/document source implements the reworked model that resolves the old List objection.

evidence_items.summary: d72b1d787a introduced the challenged collection/List wording before the issue, and 40f10d0835 later aligned active document narrative notes with Composition.section.text.
evidence_items.learned: History shows no missing FHIR-7372 source edit after the later Composition rework.

evidence_items.summary: A 2018 discussion says Composition.section.text can be used for narrative-only document sections, while domain-appropriate resources are preferable when possible.
evidence_items.learned: Community context supports the current split between document section narrative and resource/list content.
